assertions.name: A2_block_program_collapses_to_six_vars
assertions.source: block and collapsed LPs agree to 1e-12 at A = 2, 3, 4

assertions.name: A5_pairing_law_and_pure_species_zero
assertions.source: E_bind/min(Z,N) takes exactly 2 values [0.069589805, 0.070191428] over 0<=Z,N<=4 (spread 0.86%); Z=0 or N=0 gives exactly 0

assertions.name: A6_in_window_gap_is_real
assertions.source: 3 methods agree to 0.0e+00; duals valid; cheaper aggregate point exhibited

description: Reformulates the atom LP as an n-fold integer program (De Loera-Hemmecke-Onn-Weismantel, math/0605242): free = n separate local blocks min{t.x_k : G x_k >= G v_k, x_k >= 0}, atom = the same constraints aggregated into one coupling block. Aggregation is a relaxation so E_bind = free - atom >= 0 structurally, with x_p + x_n an explicit aggregate-feasible point of cost exactly free. The atom program collapses from 6^A to 6 variables (verified against the explicit block LP at A = 2,3,4), making binding the cone-crossing defect of the LP value function. At q_0 the proton and neutron optimal supports are nested ((2,3,4) and (2,3)), so both lie in one linearity cone and E_bind is an exact zero (max 5.3e-15 across 2H..16O). The mechanism is real but windowed: h in (0.47718, 0.56984), peak 0.0687 at h = 0.534, with q_0 56.2% below the lower edge. Inside the window E_bind = min(Z,N)*kappa exactly, kappa ~ 0.0696, and zero for pure-proton or pure-neutron systems. NEGATIVE for the L2 binding gap: this route does not repair the 4He miss.
caveats: THE COST FUNCTIONAL CHANGED. The n-fold form requires an ADDITIVE cost sum_k t.x_k, where the corpus's atom construction uses the multiplicative t^(x)A . x. These are different functionals, not two spellings of one. The Markov trace IS multiplicative on disjoint strand blocks (h3a_frobenius_gram_offdiagonal_probe), so the additive cost is its logarithm in spirit but not literally — log(t.x) is not linear in x, so no exact change of variables converts one program into the other. The zero reported here is a zero for the additive-Markov-cost program specifically.

The pairing law is NOT the semi-empirical mass formula. min(Z,N) = (A-|N-Z|)/2 gives a volume term and an asymmetry term with coefficients locked at ratio 1, and an asymmetry term linear in |N-Z|; the SEMF's goes as (N-Z)^2/A with an independent coefficient. The agreement claimed here is qualitative only: binding proportional to the proton-neutron pair count, and exactly zero for pure-species systems. Nothing was fitted and no B_AME value was consulted.

THIS IS THE LP RELAXATION, NOT THE IP. Everything measured here runs scipy.linprog over the continuous relaxation. The n-fold AGGREGATION structure is fully exercised — it is what produces the gap, the 6^A collapse and the pairing law — but Theorem 1.1's actual content, poly-time solvability of the INTEGER program via Graver-basis stabilisation, is untouched. Since the relaxation collapses to 6 variables it is trivially tractable, so the entire complexity question lives in the integrality not built here.

Window edges are 50-step bisections on a 1e-9 threshold against a float64 LP, so the last few digits quoted are the bisection's precision, not certified algebraic values. The interior gap (0.0687 at the peak) is 8 orders above the noise floor and is separately verified by three LP methods, dual certificates, and an explicit cheaper feasible point; the exact zeros at q_0 are 9 orders below the same floor.
